findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.assumptions: The buffer size is fixed and can be exceeded by user input. The server does not check the length of the received data before processing it.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.assumptions: The server processes the received data and executes it as a command. The client input is not sanitized before being sent to the server.

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
findings.trigger: Input containing HTML or JavaScript code
findings.assumptions: The server sends the received data back to the client without proper sanitization. The client displays the data in a web browser.

findings.title: Use of Hard-Coded Credentials
findings.assumptions: The server IP and port are hard-coded in the client application. An attacker can easily identify the server and attempt to exploit it.
